script: Rockefeller secretly destroyed his competitors using railroad rebates nobody was supposed to see. In the 1870s, Standard Oil controlled almost every refinery in America, but not through better oil. Rockefeller struck secret deals with railroads, getting massive rebates on his own shipments while smaller rivals paid full price. Worse, he got a cut of what his competitors paid too, profiting every time they tried to compete with him. Small refiners had no idea why they kept losing money on deals that should have worked. They blamed bad luck, bad management, anything but the truth. A journalist named Ida Tarbell finally exposed the scheme decades later, sparking the case that broke Standard Oil apart. Rockefeller secretly destroyed his competitors, and let the public believe he simply built a better company.

title: Rockefeller Secretly Destroyed His Competitors With Railroad Rebates
description:
Standard Oil didn't win by building a better company. Rockefeller struck secret railroad deals that profited even when his rivals tried to compete, and let the public believe otherwise for decades.
